invocation.output:
**Refused on the first attempt.** Exact reason:

> Refusing to overwrite /workspace/project/inventory.txt: it changed on disk after you read it. Another agent is working in this directory. Read the file again, re-apply your change to the current content, then write. If you only need to change part of it, prefer edit_file — it re-reads the file itself and cannot clobber a concurrent edit.

`overwrite_read_confirm=true` did not bypass it — that flag only covers "I never read this file," not "the bytes changed underneath me."

Current state on disk (unchanged, write did not land):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Content | `apples=3` / `bananas=6` / `cherries=7` / `dates=9` |
| Size | 38 bytes, 4 lines |
| mtime | 2026-10-21 10:44:24.125 UTC |

Note the mtime is **4 seconds before** your message — something touched the file between my last read and this write, which is exactly what the guard caught. Content happens to still match what I edited earlier, so nothing was corrupted; the write just never happened.

## To finish it

Say the word and I'll do it properly: read the file fresh, then `write_file` with the two kiwis/lemons lines. Or if you'd rather not wait, the same result via `edit_file` on the current content also works.
